# α task
![](images/tasks.png){style="width:200px; border-radius:5px; background:white; border: white solid 5px" fig-align="center"}

As an optional task create a new violin plot that includes the following:

- Plots the metrics:
  - "diversity_inverse_simpson" renaming it as "invsimpson"
  - "evenness_pielou" renaming it as "pielou"
  - "diversity_fisher" renaming it as "fisher"
  - Ensure they are in the order "pielou", "invsimpson", then "fisher"
- The x-axis is separated by Site (UD, MD, LD) rather than media.
  - Ensure the order is UD, MD, then LD
- Points are coloured by Media (ENV, CVP, KBC, and TSA)
  - Ensure the order is ENV, CVP, KBC, then TSA
- Include Wilcoxon paired stats comparing the Sites


::: {.callout-note}
Going to earlier code, [renaming](/rarefaction/alpha_data_frame_tidy.qmd#rename-metrics), adding new options, and rerunning the entire notebook may be useful.
:::

## Solutions

Below are expandable solution boxes showing step by step how to complete the task.

Remember:

- Please make a good attempt yourself before looking at the solutions
- Your solution might be different. As long as your solution works and you understand it that is grand. There are infinite ways to do the same thing in `R`.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Rename diversity metrics"}
Add an extra [`dplyr::rename()` function](https://neof-workshops.github.io/Tidyverse/dplyr/rename.html) along with the previous one. You will then need to rerun the jupyter-notebook.
In your own analysis it is best to do this at one time as rarefying with 1000 iterations will take much longer than with our demonstrative 10.
```{R, eval=FALSE}
#Rename
#Rename columns
#dplyr::rename(df, new_name=old_name)
alpha_df_mean <- alpha_df_mean |>
  dplyr::rename(shannon=diversity_shannon,
                invsimpson=diversity_inverse_simpson,
                pielou=evenness_pielou,
                fisher=diversity_fisher)
```
:::

The blocks in the below solution boxes should be created and run at the bottom of the jupyter-notebook.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Data frame with metrics of choice"}
Subset [long alpha diversity table created earlier in this section](/rarefaction/alpha_data_frame_tidy.qmd#long-data-frame) to contain metrics of choice.
```{R, eval=FALSE}
#To compare means we need to create a list of comparisons
#Create character vector of unique metadata values (media in this case)
uniq_media_values_chr_vec <- basic_alpha_metrics_tbl |>
    #Extract media as a vector
    dplyr::pull(media) |>
    #Convert to character
    as.character() |>
    #Unique values
    unique()
#View vector
uniq_media_values_chr_vec
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Create metadata combination list for plot stats"}
```{R,eval = FALSE}
#To compare means we need to create a list of comparisons
#Create list of site 2-way comparisons
my_comparisons <- subset_alpha_metrics_tbl |>
    #Extract site column as a vector
    dplyr::pull(site) |>
    #Convert to character
    as.character() |>
    #Unique values
    unique() |>
    #Pairwise combinations of sites
    combn(m =2, simplify=FALSE)
#Check contents and structure
my_comparisons
str(my_comparisons)
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Reorder factors and comparisons"}
```{r,eval = FALSE}
#Reorder sites, media and comparisons
#Set order of sites
subset_alpha_metrics_tbl$site <- factor(subset_alpha_metrics_tbl$site,
                                           #set order of levels
                                           levels = c("UD", "MD", "LD"))
#Set order of media
subset_alpha_metrics_tbl$media <- factor(subset_alpha_metrics_tbl$media,
                                            #set order of levels
                                            levels = c("ENV","CVP","KBC","TSA"))
#Order comparisons
my_ordered_comparisons <- my_comparisons[c(3,1,2)]
my_ordered_comparisons
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Plot with stats"}
```{R, eval = FALSE}
#Produce ggplot object of violin plot
alpha_violinplot <- ggplot(subset_alpha_metrics_tbl, aes(x = site, y = value)) +
                            ggplot2::geom_violin() +
                            ggforce::geom_sina(alpha=0.5, aes(colour=media)) +
                            ggplot2::labs(colour = "Media", x = "Site", y = "Value") +
                            ggplot2::facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free") +
                            #Add comparisons
                            ggpubr::stat_compare_means(comparisons = my_ordered_comparisons)
#Save ggplot2 object with ggsave
ggsave(filename = "./Alpha_diversity_rarefy_iters_site_violinplot_pairwise_wilcox.png", plot = alpha_violinplot,
      device = "png", dpi = 300, units = "mm", height = 200, width = 250)
#Display plot
IRdisplay::display_png(file = "./Alpha_diversity_rarefy_iters_site_violinplot_pairwise_wilcox.png")
```
:::

## Recap

- Produced __alpha diversity__ values through __iterative rarefaction__
- Created a long data frame containing metadata and specified __alpha diversity__ metrics
- Visualised the group differences of __alpha diversity__ metrics with violin plots
- Embedded paired Wilcoxon p-values in our violin plots

With these skills and knowledge you will be able to carry out thorough investigations of __alpha diversity__ in your future research.
